text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: No mass roundup of extremists.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reassures Palestinian President Yasser Arafat over Oslo.
- Three more soldiers wounded in Hizbollah attack.
- Easing closure is a calculated risk, Mordechai says.
- One killed, 11 wounded as soldiers fire on Palestinian marchers.
- Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to meet U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in Cairo.
- 16-year-old suicide bomber price: $50,000.
- Cable and Wireless wants larger Bezeq stake "but not majority share".
- U.S.-based Southwestern Bell will seek more business here.
- Golden Lines to spend 500 million shekels on infrastructure.
- Tender for Mount Carmel tunnel complex due to be published within a few weeks.
- United Mizrahi Bank intends to sell branches in Switzerland and Britain.
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel: Increase in minimum wage would be disastrous.
- Transport Minister Yitzhak Levy proposes ending Maman cargo monopoly.
GLOBES
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor: A change in monetary policy is required within two months.
- Bank Leumi discusses sale of Africa-Israel to Lev Leviev, a leading figure in the local diamond industry. Profit to Israeli businessmen Mordechai Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer about $16 million.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu to Arafat: Delay of Hebron accord will result in explosion. Head of Shin Bet gets an order to prepare for redeployment in Hebron -- soon.
MAARIV
- Three wounded in Lebanon attack; Israeli army discussions on problem of protecting tanks.
- Netanyahu to Arafat: After Hebron we'll evacuate more territories. Negotiations resume between Israel and the Palestinian Authority -- and again there's talk of an agreement on Hebron soon.
HAARETZ
- Egypt proposes Lebanon arrangement: Israel will withdraw, can respond harshly if attacked.
- Islamic Jihad leader: Because of the security measures Israel took, we put off carrying out an attack.
- Assessment: Arafat will likely ignore the process and announce establishment of a state.
- Kach man Noam Federman arrested without trial for two months.
- Survey: 60 percent of the secular Jews in Jerusalem consider leaving holy city, a majority because of the ultra-Orthodox.
- Investigators who checked Soviet archives: Seven million Jews perished in the Holocaust.
